comparison: Both strongly support claims C14-C19 regarding hMT+ GABA correlations with BDT and SI. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor and specificity controls; peer reviewers praised the comprehensive approach but noted sample size as a minor drawback. Both rate evidence as convincing/supported.

Perfect agreement on claims C22-C24 regarding behavioral validation of motion suppression and intelligence. Both evaluations accept the findings as supported with appropriate controls and replication of prior work (Melnick et al., 2013).

Perfect agreement on claims C25-C27 regarding connectivity with fronto-parietal networks. Both accept the findings as supported and consistent with intelligence literature. OpenEval requests additional effect size reporting; peer reviewers had no critiques.

Perfect agreement on claims C28, C29, C43 regarding specific connectivity-GABA relationships. Both accept the statistical rigor (FDR correction) and specificity to GABA. OpenEval notes the opposite directionality requires mechanistic explanation; peer reviewers treated findings as novel contributions without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C30, C31, C33, C34 regarding BA46 mediation model. Both support the findings. OpenEval notes the 95% CI barely excludes zero and recommends tempering causal interpretation; peer reviewers characterized evidence as 'convincing' without raising these concerns.

Both address claim C32 (BA6 mediation). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to incomplete statistical reporting; peer reviewers accepted the findings as SUPPORTED without critique, treating differential connectivity patterns as an 'interesting finding.'

Both address claim C21 regarding GABA-glutamate correlations. OpenEval supports as validation of MRS measurements; peer reviewers also accepted, noting it supports specificity of GABAergic mechanisms in the study's hypothesis.

Both address claim C35 regarding differential connectivity patterns. OpenEval supports but notes mechanistic interpretation remains speculative; peer reviewers accepted without challenge as contributing to understanding of sensory cortex GABA and frontal regions.

Perfect agreement on claims C11, C12, C52, C53 (main conclusions). Both strongly support the overarching conclusions. OpenEval recommends tempering causal language given correlational design; peer reviewers explicitly stated evidence is 'convincing' and 'advances understanding' without this caveat.

Disagreement on claims C5, C6, C10 regarding V1 versus hMT+ in motion perception. OpenEval supports the theoretical framework (C1-C10) as appropriately cited; peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, challenging the claim that motion is associated with hMT+ 'but not in EVC' as 'incorrect and too rough,' citing V1's established role in motion perception.

Both address background claims C1-C4, C7-C8 establishing theoretical framework. Both support these foundational concepts as appropriately cited and consistent with established literature. High agreement on rationale.

Both address claims C13, C54-C56, C61 regarding participants. Both support the design. OpenEval notes sample size justification is simplistic and attrition rate substantial; peer reviewers noted sample size as 'relatively low' but adequate, with no other concerns.

Partial overlap on VOI placement methods (C58-C60, C71-C72). OpenEval supports with minor limitation noted (lack of functional localization for all subjects); peer reviewers praised sophisticated techniques with only sample size as concern. Both support methodological rigor.
Both address behavioral measures C62-C65. Perfect agreement that measures are appropriate, well-validated, and follow established methods. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Both address MRS methodology (C66-C70, C73-C74, C76-C77). Perfect agreement supporting state-of-the-art methods. OpenEval emphasizes technical rigor; peer reviewers praised '7T high-resolution MRS' and 'sophisticated techniques' as study strengths.

Both address fMRI/statistical methods (C78-C81). Perfect agreement supporting appropriate methodology. OpenEval notes methods adequately described for reproducibility; peer reviewers accepted without critique as part of overall sound approach.

Both address discussion/interpretation claims C36-C47. OpenEval supports but notes some interpretations are speculative (resting-state vs task-based, attentional effects); peer reviewers accepted discussion without challenge, focusing critiques only on V1 motion perception claims.

Both address claims C48-C51 regarding extension to broader MD system. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting claims are speculative and require additional evidence; peer reviewers accepted as SUPPORTED without raising concerns about the speculative nature of these broader implications.

OpenEval addresses claim C44 (local vs global connectivity contribution to SI) as SUPPORTED but notes relative contributions not quantified; peer reviewers included C44 in broader discussion acceptance without specific critique. Minor overlap with different emphasis.

Minimal overlap on claim C20 (no V1 GABA-BDT correlation). OpenEval includes C20 in comprehensive support of specificity findings; peer reviewers separately accepted C20-C21 as supporting GABAergic specificity. Agreement on interpretation.
